answer: The modeller was Robert Sanderson, who raised this in April 2017 (thread t1004, 'E78 Collection vs E19 Physical Object'): E19's scope note claims to cover 'all aggregates of objects made for functional purposes of whatever kind', E78 Curated Holding is such an aggregation, yet E78 is not a subclass of E19 (both descend independently from E18/E24), which he called a logical inconsistency ('All aggregations of objects are E19s. E78s are aggregations of objects. E78s are not E19s.'). Several different fixes were proposed. (1) Sanderson's own preferred fix: make E78 a subclass of E22 Man-Made Object, since E22 is already a subclass of both E19 and E24 -- the 'simplest change' to give E78 an E19 ancestor. He also floated a more comprehensive alternative: create a new class below E19 for 'Sets', move property P57 to it, and make E78 a child of that new class and of E24. (2) A non-hierarchy fix he also proposed: reword E78's scope note to drop the restrictive 'over time for a specific purpose... collection development plan' language, and change the clause distinguishing E78 from E19 to reference collection plans rather than physical binding/functionality. (3) Stephen Stead rejected any re-parenting: he argued E78 must be able to hold curated 'features' (not just objects), so forcing it under E22 (objects only) would wrongly exclude features; where an instance really is both an E19 and an E78, he said 'multiple instantiation is the solution, not tinkering with the class definitions'. (4) Christian-Emil Smith Ore likewise leaned toward multiple instantiation as the practical fix and, rather than committing to a hierarchy change, challenged Sanderson to formally raise a new issue with a fully worked-out, logically consistent hierarchy and draft scope notes. (5) Martin Doerr (the CRM editor) rejected the premise that there was a bug to fix at all, invoking the Open World principle: auction lots and hoards are simply E19s (they do have functionality), and things like 'the set of objects on a photo' that lack an identity condition are simply outside CRM's current scope and can be added by users without violating compatibility -- 'the CRM is NOT a data format'. No hierarchy change resulted from this thread: it is marked 'unresolved' in the concept chronology, and the current ontology (v7.1.3) still lists E78 Curated Holding as a subclass only of E24, not of E19 or E22. A later, related proposal (Issue 442, 2020, thread t1405) again left E78's parent as E24 and instead only reworded the scope note to add explicit identity criteria distinguishing E78 (identity via continuity of a development plan) from E19 (identity via the constellation of physically/functionally bound parts) -- a scope-note clarification, not a re-parenting.

notes: Thread t1004 fully documents the debate and all proposed fixes; the concept E78 chronology independently confirms the 2017-04-14 episode is tagged '[unresolved]' and the current ontology entry still shows E78 as subclass of only E24, confirming no hierarchy change. Thread t1405 (Issue 442, 2020) was checked to see if a later fix changed the hierarchy -- it did not; it only clarified the scope note's identity criteria.
